final_label: D1 after a rewarded a1->S1 (common) trial; at window start, rewarded D1 with belief favoring S1

with_model_outputs.label: D1 after reward, agent about to choose a1 (rewarded a1->S1 common)
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2) and only when a reward is shown (in_rew == 1), and almost only when the agent will choose a1 on this trial (its own upcoming choice, which it computes; not an unobservable random outcome). Observed-history view: it is the D1 right after an a1 choice that reached S1 by a common transition and was rewarded (prev_action==1 & prev_common==1 & in_rew==1: precision 0.999, recall 0.74; the missing recall is almost all window-first trials whose previous trial is outside the window). It does NOT fire after rewarded rare transitions (a1->S2 or a2->S1), after any a2 trial, or after no reward. Recorded the upcoming-choice predicate (dev F1 0.95, mass recall 0.998) because it covers window-first trials; it is effectively a reward-at-S1 / stay-on-a1 signal. Magnitude is roughly constant (median 2.07 of max 2.63); weaker activations are rarer cases such as when the agent then switches or the policy logit toward a1 is moderate.

issues: The recorded predicate (phase==D1 & in_rew==1 & action==1) leaves out a systematic false-positive class: D1 after a rewarded a1->S2 RARE trial where the agent then stays on a1. The predicate is true on 6332 such dev steps and the feature fires on 0.3% of them. The misses output on test shows the pattern directly ('a1 S2R' rewarded, then '*r1* a1 S1c' inactive). This class makes up most of the 10186 test false positives. So 'about to choose a1' is not what drives the feature; the observed history is.

The claim 'does NOT fire after any a2 trial / after rewarded rare a2->S1' is only partly true. After a rewarded a2->S1 rare trial where the agent then switches to a1, the feature fires on 54% of the 4340 such steps (dev). The class is small, about 2.9% recall and 0.5% of activation mass, but the 54% firing rate is a real exception to that blanket claim.

Verified claims: the feature fires only at D1 (0 activations at GO and D2) and only when in_rew==1. The observed history predicate prev_action==1 & prev_common==1 & in_rew==1 has dev precision 0.999 and recall 0.743. The missed recall is almost all window-opening trials (prev_action==-1: recall 0.228, and precision 0.963 when combined with action==1). It does not fire after a rewarded a1->S2 rare trial (0.0 recall).

The label leads with the upcoming choice ('agent about to choose a1'), which overclaims: a1 choices after a rare-rewarded a1 trial do not activate it. The core signal is observed: reward just received at S1 after a common a1 transition.

Better predicate: observed history, with the upcoming choice used only on window-opening trials where the history is unknown. Test P 0.990 / R 0.964 / F1 0.977. Adding the a2->S1 rare-rewarded -> a1 case gives test P 0.967 / R 0.990 / F1 0.978 / mass recall 0.999, compared with the recorded predicate's test F1 0.949.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 right after a rewarded a1->S1 common trial (reward obtained at S1 via a1); not after a rewarded a1->S2 rare trial, even if the agent stays on a1

with_model_outputs.final_label: D1 right after a rewarded a1->S1 common trial (reward obtained at S1 via a1); not after a rewarded a1->S2 rare trial, even if the agent stays on a1

label: D1 after a rewarded a1->S1 (common) trial; at window start, rewarded D1 with belief favoring S1
explanation: Fires only at D1 and only when the reward input is 1. Within that, it fires when the previous trial was a1 with a common transition to S1 that was rewarded (the classic win-stay-for-a1 signal). On window-start steps, where the previous trial is not in the window, the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good (>0.5) stands in. Silent after a2 choices and after rare a1->S2 transitions. Adding rewarded a2->S1 rare trials with high belief only raises dev F1 from 0.958 to 0.960. Magnitude modulation not checked.

issues: Claims check out: 100% D1 and 100% in_rew==1. The core clause (rewarded a1->S1) has test precision 0.999. After a rewarded rare a1->S2 trial precision is 0.004. After a rewarded rare a2->S1 trial precision is 0.20, recall 0.035 (minor).

The window-start clause is the weak part (precision 0.85, recall 0.20). Most false positives are rel==-3 steps where the agent then chooses a2. Using action==1 there gives precision 0.96, so belief>0.5 is an imperfect stand-in for the unseen previous trial. This is expected and small (3.1% of mass missed).
